question_text:
A steel cable 0.5 in. in diameter has a yield strength of 70,000 psi. The density of steel is about $7.87 \mathrm{~g} / \mathrm{cm}^{3}$. Based on the data in Table, determine (a) the maximum load that the steel cable can support without yielding, (b) the diameter of a cold-worked aluminum-manganese alloy (3004-H18) required to support the same load as the steel, and (c) the weight per foot of the steel cable versus the aluminum alloy cable. The yield strength of the aluminum alloy is $36,000 \mathrm{psi}$ and its density is $2.70 \mathrm{~g} / \mathrm{cm}^{3}$. Give your answer as a tuple (maximum load without yielding in lb, diameter of aluminum alloy in in, weight per foot of steel cable in lb, weight per foot of aluminum alloy cable in lb).

response:
## Solution

**(a) Maximum load without yielding**

The load at yielding equals the yield strength times the cross-sectional area:

$$A_{\text{steel}} = \frac{\pi d^2}{4} = \frac{\pi(0.5)^2}{4} = 0.19635\ \text{in}^2$$

$$F_{\max} = \sigma_y A = 70{,}000 \times 0.19635 \approx 13{,}744\ \text{lb}$$

**(b) Diameter of 3004-H18 aluminum alloy for the same load**

$$A_{\text{Al}} = \frac{F_{\max}}{\sigma_{y,\text{Al}}} = \frac{13{,}744}{36{,}000} = 0.3818\ \text{in}^2$$

$$d_{\text{Al}} = \sqrt{\frac{4A_{\text{Al}}}{\pi}} \approx 0.697\ \text{in}$$

**(c) Weight per foot**

Converting density: $\rho\ [\text{lb/in}^3] = \rho\ [\text{g/cm}^3]\times \dfrac{(2.54)^3}{453.592}$

- Steel: $\rho = 0.2843\ \text{lb/in}^3$, volume/ft $= A_s \times 12 = 2.356\ \text{in}^3$
  $$W_{\text{steel}} = 0.2843 \times 2.356 \approx 0.670\ \text{lb/ft}$$

- Aluminum: $\rho = 0.0975\ \text{lb/in}^3$, volume/ft $= A_{\text{Al}} \times 12 = 4.581\ \text{in}^3$
  $$W_{\text{Al}} = 0.0975 \times 4.581 \approx 0.447\ \text{lb/ft}$$

The aluminum cable is lighter per foot despite its larger diameter, illustrating the weight advantage of aluminum alloys.
